sentences.text: This pterosaur had a skull measuring 30 centimeters in length and a wingspan reaching two meters.
A distinctive crest ran along the top of its premaxilla, the front part of the upper jaw.
This crest consisted of vertical trabeculae, a structure originally mistaken for the filter teeth of another genus.
The lower jaw, or dentary, held sixteen sockets for teeth, although the actual teeth are no longer present.
Researchers initially thought the fossil belonged to the genus Pterodaustro before realizing it was unique.
The name references the long wing finger typical of pterosaurs found in the Cordillera Domeyko region.
The genus was formally named in the year 2000 by David Martill, Eberhard Frey, Guillermo Chong Diaz, and Charles Michael Bell.
The species name ceciliae honors geologist Cecilia Demargasso for her collaboration with the research team.
Scientists assigned this animal to the Dsungaripteridae family because of its elevated tooth sockets.
Domeykodactylus lived during the Early Cretaceous in the Santa Ana Formation of Antofagasta, Chile.
It existed between 143.1 and 100.5 million years ago, spanning from the Berriasian to the Albian stages.
